title: DiffusionGemma Technical Report
authors: DiffusionGemma Team (core contributors listed alphabetically; leads Sebastian Flennerhag, Brendan O'Donoghue, George Scrivener, Shantanu Thakoor)
date: August 2026 (arXiv v1 31 July 2026; the e-print is dated 4 August 2026); the weights were released on 9 June 2026

code.title: google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it
code.note: the open weights (Apache 2.0, created on Hugging Face on 9 June 2026; 583,543 downloads on 3 October 2026), with reference implementations in Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM and a LoRA finetuning toolkit built on Hackable Diffusion

takeaway: First open-weights text diffusion model that is fast and genuinely capable: Gemma 4 26B A4B warm-started from AR weights with under 10% of the AR token budget hits ~20 tokens per forward pass and ~1,500 TPS on one H100 (7.1x its AR baseline) via block-AR encoder-decoder decoding plus a unified SD-RL stage, at a real but bounded quality tax.

headline.d: Gemma 4 with multi-token prediction: 1.40; speculative decoding in general: 3 to 6

headline.k: one H100, FP8, one request at a time
GPQA-Diamond against its own AR parent
headline.d: the quality tax: 9 points here, 19 on AIME 2026, under 1 on GSM8K

verdict: Believe the speed at one request per GPU: it follows from the paper's own per-step timing and tokens per pass, and the code is public. Treat the comparisons with other systems (Mercury 2 through an API, LLaDA on 8 B200s, the MTP baseline measured on a different benchmark) and the crossover at about 32 users as rough, and the quality gap as real.

resources.t: DiffusionGemma: the first diffusion LLM natively supported in vLLM
resources.by: vLLM team and Google DeepMind, 10 June 2026
resources.n: how one set of weights runs as a causal encoder and a bidirectional decoder inside a serving engine: the per-sequence causal flag, entropy-bounded denoising and self-conditioning as implemented.
the weights, licence, chat template and usage.

resources.n: the entropy-bounded sampler that Algorithm 1 instantiates, from the masked-diffusion side.
the continuous-time Markov chain framework of Section 2 (probability paths, the Euler step in footnote 1).
the closed text diffusion model the paper names as part of the landscape it set out to open up.
the closed diffusion model DiffusionGemma is compared with; reports about 1,000 tokens per second on Blackwell GPUs.

kb.n: the issue that covered this report, with the animation of one 256-token block decoded autoregressively, with speculative decoding and with DiffusionGemma, in passes and in milliseconds. This page does not repeat it.

2020: the continuous diffusion foundation, with a live toy; DiffusionGemma uses its discrete-state descendant (CTMC, discrete flow matching, multinomial corruption) instead of Gaussian diffusion in embedding space, which the paper argues breaks likelihood bounds under rounding.
2021: diffusion made cheap by moving where it runs; the image-side analogue of trading steps for cost.
2018: masked and random token replacement in pretraining is the single-step ancestor that discrete diffusion generalises into a multi-step Markov process.
2019: the bidirectional-encoder, causal-decoder layout that DiffusionGemma inverts.
another conversion of Gemma decoder weights into an encoder-decoder, the conventional way round.
MoE serving background: the expert transfer that keeps sparse AR decoding cheap becomes DiffusionGemma's largest per-step overhead (84 against 8 unique experts per layer per canvas).
the memory-bound serving analysis that motivates the whole approach; DiffusionGemma ships as a vLLM reference implementation with asynchronous scheduling.
the RLVR baseline recipe; SD·RL is its diffusion-native counterpart, with sampler distillation fused into the RL stage and conciseness instead of length growth as the emergent behaviour.
the adapters the released finetuning toolkit uses (rank 8 for Sudoku, rank 4 for PubMedQA).

topics.n: text diffusion and world models: DiffusionGemma is the strongest open-weights entry in the 2026 AR-initialised block-diffusion recipe described there (Mercury, Gemini Diffusion, LLaDA 2.x), and confirms the pattern of block diffusion over a causal context to keep KV-cache reuse.
memory-bound decoding, speculative decoding and batch-size economics.
the Gemma 4 family this model is converted from, and Gemini Diffusion.
